label: early copy phase when the current or next output is one of w/0/t/q/g/2
explanation: Active on about 5% of steps. It is strongest at the <DEL> step (17% rate, 34% of mass) and in the first few copy steps (recall_idx 0-3), and it falls off later in the copy. It is never active at t=0-1, and it is weak in the original phase, which holds 18% of mass, mostly in the last few inputs before <DEL>. Activation depends on output identity: w is by far the strongest (45% rate when output), followed by 0, t, q, g and 2, then a and o. The first original token matters in the same way at <DEL>, and the strongest examples are sequences starting with w at <DEL> or the first copy step. The predicate (early copy or delim, current or next output in {w,0,t,q,g,2}) reaches F1 of about 0.38 on dev with mass recall of about 0.67. Precision is low (about 0.28), so this looks like a graded, distributed code over upcoming output identity rather than a crisp rule. It does not fire on late copy steps or at the start of the sequence.
